mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding 6 months signals a tightening monetary regime, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of 2% or more signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 8% for two consecutive months signals labor market distress, which erodes consumer purchasing power and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not negative in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent acceleration in industrial production (INDPRO) and a deceleration in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1 standard deviation from their 12-month mean indicates a shift from construction to manufacturing intensity, which historically precedes equity reallocation toward cyclicals and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > +1σ and HOUST < -1σ in the same month
regime_hint: transition from housing to manufacturing cycle
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive (< +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the monetary base (RSAFS) of more than 5% month-over-month, in the absence of a corresponding decline in broad money, signals liquidity draining from the financial system, which increases risk premiums and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS MoM change < -5% and M2 growth > 0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not negative in at least 70% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) and personal income (implied from PAYEMS growth) of at least 0.4% month-over-month signals strong demand-pull inflation, which typically precedes central bank tightening and negative equity risk premia, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the labor force participation rate (implied by UNRATE and PAYEMS dynamics) above 63% for three consecutive months signals a tightening labor market, which boosts wage growth and corporate costs, ultimately producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as earnings expectations rise.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in housing starts (HOUST) below its 12-month moving average by more than 10% for four consecutive months signals a protracted housing downturn, which historically correlates with negative consumer sentiment and reduced durable goods demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < 90% of 12-month moving average for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
